openSpielGameParameters.description: Game parameters for Open Spiel game.

openSpielGameString.description: The full game string including parameters.

presetHands.description: Repeated poker only. List of per-hand chance action sequences to use instead of random chance.

runTimeout.description: Maximum runtime (seconds) of an episode (not necessarily DONE).

savePrompt.description: If true, the LLM prompt produced by the harness is included as a 'prompt' field on the action returned by core_harness, which causes it to be persisted in the episode replay. Defaults to false to keep replays small.

seed.description: Integer currently only used for selecting starting position.

strictMode.description: If true, agents must return only {'submission': int} (no extra fields like 'thoughts'), and per-agent TIMEOUT/ERROR/INVALID counts as a loss for the offending agent only — other agents win. If false (default), any agent error halts and voids the entire episode, matching the lenient research-mode behavior.

useImage.description: If true, indicates the observation is intended to be rendered as an image. Note that currently the agent harness is responsible for the actual rendering; no image is passed in the observation.

useOpenings.description: Whether to start from a position in an opening book.

currentPlayer.description: ID of player whose turn it is.

legalActionStrings.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action strings. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

legalActions.description: List of OpenSpiel legal action integers. Only included if includeLegalActions is true.

openSpielGameName.description: Short name of the OpenSpiel game.

playerId.description: ID of the agent receiving this observation.

serializedGameAndState.description: Enables reconstructing the Game and State objects.

remainingOverageTime.description: Total remaining banked time (seconds) that can be used in excess of per-step actTimeouts -- agent is disqualified with TIMEOUT status when this drops below 0.

In Connect 4 (or its generalization Connect X), the center columns provide the most flexibility for creating multiple winning threats in horizontal, vertical, and diagonal directions simultaneously. 

Placing an 'o' in column 3 stacks directly above the existing 'x', claiming control of the central vertical line early while also opening up strong potential for horizontal and diagonal connections. This is a standard high-value response in opening play. Columns 2 or 4 are reasonable alternatives for diagonal setups but are slightly less central and versatile overall.

action.thoughts:
The board is mostly empty, with only three pieces placed so far: an 'o' at row 4/col 3 and two adjacent 'x's at row 5/col 2 and row 5/col 3. No player has a forcing threat (i.e., three-in-a-row with an open fourth spot), so the focus is on long-term positional strength.

In Connect 4, the center column is the highest-value location because it participates in the largest number of potential winning lines (vertical, both diagonals, and horizontal). Column 3 already contains an 'o' directly above the bottom 'x', so dropping another 'o' there builds a vertical stack of two 'o's while claiming the next center spot. This creates immediate potential for vertical/diagonal threats on subsequent turns and denies the opponent easy use of the same column.

Alternative moves (e.g., col 2 or col 4 to "block" the 'x' pair) are unnecessary because the 'x's only have two adjacent pieces and no immediate win path. Placing on the edges (col 0/1/5/6) cedes central control without compensation. Thus column 3 is the highest-value, optimal choice under standard Connect 4 heuristics.

Final Answer: 3

This creates an immediate fork: on x's next turn, playing in column 1 or column 5 would complete four-in-a-row horizontally and win the game. No single move by o can block both threats at once.

- Although x can ignore the new threat and win immediately via one of the open ends (columns 1 or 5), this move still maximizes our position and forces x to respond correctly to avoid a loss on the subsequent turn.

Every possible column leads to a loss against perfect play, but column 3 is the strongest continuation.
